turns.content: Two planets transit rotating stars in central transits. The stars have the same spectral type, apparent magnitude, and activity; Star 1 has twice Star 2's radius and rotates three times faster, while Planet 1 has four times Planet 2's radius. Which in-transit spectroscopic radial-velocity effect should be compared?
For a central transit, state the approximate semi-amplitude scaling of this effect with planet radius, stellar radius, and stellar rotation speed.
Compute the ratio (R_p/R_star)_1 divided by (R_p/R_star)_2 from the stated planet and stellar radii.

Combine the squared comparison factor established above with the stellar rotation-speed factor to obtain the requested system-1/system-2 observable ratio. The equal stellar properties allow their noise and photon-collection factors to be ignored in this comparison.
Using the comparison obtained above, which system should receive the limited observing time first, and what quantitative advantage supports that priority?
Verify that the common stellar properties and central-transit geometry have been applied consistently with the radius and rotation-speed factors used in the priority comparison.
Name the system that should receive the limited observing time first, and justify the priority from the transit-signal scaling and common-noise assumptions.
